mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the capillary networks was most worthwhile: it explained that blood must exchange substances with tissues, not merely pass by them. That connects circulation to the cells' need for supplies.

leastWorthwhile.text: Filling the circuit felt the most routine. It was a clear and necessary step, but its result was predictable.

surprise.text: I found it interesting that cells in the heart start its repeating electrical rhythm without a separate brain order for every beat.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly arbitrary; each had a stated role in the pump or circuit. Several later choices were the only offered combinations, so they felt more like assembly than decisions.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter to see how circulation connects to the working arm, though I would hope for more meaningful choices. The explanations made the assembled system interesting despite the predictable sequence.
